reasoning: Revision round. Starting price ~$98.4 (Twelve Data intraday 2026-10-21 after the Q3 print [30]), not the $102.45 close or round 1's $99.8. Facts: Q3 sales $13.0B (+7.0% comparable), adj EPS $1.42 (adj operating margin 23.4%: GAAP 1,358 + specified 1,693; net interest 297; other income ~166), FY26 EPS $5.50-5.55, comparable growth cut to ~6%, CGM +7.7% with diabetes guided low-mid single digit, Nutrition spin by end-2027 [1,5,6]. Supervisor findings acted on: interest 4.4% with other income in corporate_ebit (and stripped from EBITDA); SBC no longer deducted twice; DOJ $384.2M settlement added [28]; Diagnostics margins cut to 19-21% (Exact high teens); BAX dropped from the peer median (18.8x) and the P/E re-argued from the segment mix at 17.0x; Medicare CGM competitive bidding priced into FY28 devices growth and the multiple [29]. My own additions: remaining NEC claims at an expected -$750M after tax (12,700 infants still pending [27]), H2'26 settlements moved to adjustments (the engine only counted half of FY26 other_uses), and ~$400M separation costs. Alternative-lane evidence (unchanged, colour not numbers): independent writers were bullish at $84-101 on a decade-low multiple and a diabetes re-rating [11-16] - that thesis weakened again; GlobalData share data with Dexcom's 11-13% guide implies CGM share drift [9,23]; patient forums and recall trackers on Libre 3 feed the litigation estimate [19-22]; OTC Lingo is small [17,18,25,26]. Model: FY27/FY28 adj EPS ~$6.02/$6.62 (consensus $6.08/$6.74, -1% / -2%), valued at 17.0x NTM P/E and 13.5x NTM EV/EBITDA less ~$2.4B after-tax litigation/separation cash; engine base horizon value $107.56 (P/E leg $108.86, EV/EBITDA leg $105.61). Ladder: the engine's research median ($105.5) blended half-and-half with the spot price grown ~3.3% (expected price return ~6.5% = ~9% cost of equity less ~2.5% dividend yield, less ~3% lognormal mean-to-median gap; today's price beats every blend as a forecast) gives a median ~$104; lognormal sigma 0.25 (realized 27%), with a 12% branch where the Nutrition spin completes before the horizon and the quote is ~8.5% lower (NutritionCo ~1.9B EBITDA x ~11x less ~5.5B debt = ~15B / 1,730 = ~$8.7/share; judgment). Bear/base/bull $78 / $108 / $136 (engine) at 25/55/20%. Lane share: 16 of 30 sources are alternative-lane; excluding the 7 company filings/releases used only for basic reported facts (exempt per the brief) it is 16 of 23 (70%). Research limited: X/Reddit not reachable via search, no new post-print alternative-lane coverage found, the 10-K segment note was not readable. [citation gate 2026-10-21: Diagnostics FY2027 +12.8% (the build had used the FY2025 ex-Cancer base and dropped ~$214M; was +11.0%), FY2028 +6.15%; engine base $107.96 (P/E $109.25, EV/EBITDA $106.02; was $107.56). Tax 15.5% and SBC $664M relabelled/re-cited. View unchanged; ladder unchanged]

model_inputs.structure_note: Value is carried by a 4-segment driver build (Nutrition, Diagnostics incl. Exact/Cancer Dx, EPD, Medical Devices) on adjusted EBIT (after SBC, before acquired-intangible amortization and specified items), plus ~$650M pa other income as corporate_ebit, valued with two horizon multiples on the build's own NTM figures: P/E 17.0x (weight 0.6; the most accurate single method per the playbook) and EV/EBITDA 13.5x on operating EBITDA (0.4). No DCF leg (ABT not in dcf_policy.name_weights). Litigation, the DOJ settlement and separation costs are equity-level adjustments. SOTP not used as a leg: the Nutrition spin is roughly value-neutral to holders and I lack sourced standalone nutrition/generics multiples; the P/E is built from the segment mix instead.
model_inputs.gap_note: For Kilian: (1) Nutrition separation 'by the end of next year' (CFO on the Q3 call); if it completes before 2027-10-20 (I put ~12%), the ABT quote on the horizon date excludes NutritionCo (~$8-9/share), which the ladder shades for but the consolidated fair value does not. (2) Segment margins are after allocated corporate cost and my estimates (10-K segment note not readable through the tools); the group margin is anchored to the FY26 EPS guide and Q3 reconciliation. (3) The 17.0x P/E is a judgment from the segment profit mix against a bimodal peer set (median 18.8x without BAX, 17.1x with it); each 1x is ~$6.6/share - flagged as a >5% judgment call. (4) Remaining NEC claims are carried at their expected cost (-$750M after tax), a judgment from the first settlement batch.
